1.title: AI-Assisted Development and Managed AI Services
1.text: Welcome to Module four: A I-Assisted Development and Managed A I Services. It covers the exam area Domain one: Development with A W S Services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Use A I-assisted development tools to generate, review and optimize code (one point one.nine). Integrate managed A W S A I services into applications (one point one.ten). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain one: Development with A W S Services (thirty percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: AI-assisted development
1.text: A I-assisted development. A I-assisted development means using A I tools inside the development workflow to write, review and improve code. The guide names these uses. Spec-driven code generation. Write a specification first; the tool turns it into tasks and code. Intelligent code completion. Suggestions while you type. Automated code review. The tool flags bugs, style and risk in a change. Refactoring suggestions. Cleaner structure, same behavior. Security scanning. Find vulnerabilities and secrets in code.

1.title: AI-assisted development, continued
1.text: A I-assisted development. The figure shows this: Spec-driven development: requirements, design, tasks, code and review.

1.title: Kiro and spec-driven development
1.text: Kiro and spec-driven development. Kiro is A W S's agentic development environment. Its main ideas. Specs. A feature is described as requirements, design and tasks; the agent works through the tasks. Steering files. Project rules (conventions, structure, standards) the agent follows every time. Hooks. Automations triggered by events (for example, on file save run a check). Exam tip: Spec-driven equals write the intent first, then generate. A I output is a draft: the developer reviews, tests and owns the result. Good practice: review generated code, run tests, scan for security issues, never paste secrets or personal data into prompts, and keep a human in the loop for risky changes.

1.title: Managed AI services in applications
1.text: Managed A I services in applications. The exam covers calling managed A I services from application code, not choosing models or designing R A G. Amazon Bedrock. Managed access to foundation models through an A P I; no servers to run. Amazon Bedrock Agent Core. Services to run and operate A I agents securely (runtime, gateway, identity, memory, observability). Amazon Quick. A I-powered assistant and business intelligence for users.

1.title: Calling Bedrock from code
1.text: Calling Bedrock from code. Runtime A P I. Use the Bedrock Runtime client: Invoke Model, or the model-independent Converse A P I; both have streaming versions. Permission. The caller's I A M role needs bedrock Invoke Model (and streaming equivalents) on the model. Model access. Access to a model must be enabled for the account. Errors. Throttling and quota errors: retry with backoff; handle timeouts. Responses. Parse the Jason body or the stream of chunks. Exam tip: The exam tests using A I tools and managed A I services, not choosing models or designing R A G. If an option is about model selection, it is out of scope.

1.title: Calling Bedrock from code, continued
1.text: Calling Bedrock from code. The figure shows this: An application calling a managed A I service through the S D K with an I A M role. Exam tip: "Add a generative feature without managing infrastructure" equals Amazon Bedrock called through the S D K with an I A M role. Out of scope: Polly, Rekognition, Sage Maker A I, Strands Agents.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team writes a feature description first, then lets an A I tool produce tasks and code from it. Which approach is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Spec-driven development. Spec-driven development starts from a specification.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which action reflects good practice with A I-generated code? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Review it, run tests and scan it for security issues. Generated code is a draft; the developer reviews, tests and scans it.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An application must add text generation without running any servers. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Amazon Bedrock called through the S D K. Bedrock gives managed A P I access to foundation models.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A Lambda function calling Bedrock fails with an access denied error. What is the most likely fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Add bedrock:Invoke Model for the model to the function's execution role. The caller needs permission to invoke the model.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which Bedrock A P I is model-independent and supports multi-turn conversations? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Converse. The Converse A P I gives a consistent interface across models.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which item describes a Kiro steering file? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A project rule file the agent follows every time. Steering files hold conventions and standards the agent applies.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name three A I-assisted development uses from the guide. Answer: For example code generation, automated code review and security scanning. Question two. What are the three parts of a Kiro spec? Answer: Requirements, design and tasks. Question three. What is Amazon Bedrock? Answer: Managed A P I access to foundation models.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which I A M action lets a role call a model? Answer: bedrock:Invoke Model. Question five. Is selecting a foundation model on the exam? Answer: No, it is out of scope. Question six. Who owns A I-generated code? Answer: The developer, who must review and test it.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. A I-assisted development: spec-driven generation, completion, review, refactoring, security scanning. Kiro: specs (requirements, design, tasks), steering files, hooks. Bedrock: managed foundation models via Invoke Model or Converse; I A M role; backoff on throttling. Human in the loop: review, test, scan; no secrets in prompts.
